concept.name: Data normalization
concept.definition: A broad transformation that puts observations into a chosen scale or norm so features can be compared or consumed reliably by a model.
concept.intuition: It controls what information the model receives and in what numerical representation.
concept.mechanics: Fit transformation parameters on training observations and apply the stored mapping unchanged to validation, test, and live rows.
concept.failure_modes: Fitting the operation on the full dataset leaks future information; revisions, outliers, and missing values can also distort results.
concept.misconceptions: A cleaner or rescaled dataset is not automatically more truthful; transformations must preserve timing and economic meaning.
concept.example: Each return vector is divided by its L2 norm before a similarity model, while the fitted pipeline is reused out of sample.
